This research is considered to be the second and last episode in the field of non-traditional human bodies, where the first part was published under the title "Ancient human bodies on the effects of pre-Trearch and the early era in Egypt through the sights of the fish, scenes and the representation of enemies and prisoners."
Various monuments - whether in the art of sculpture or in the art of engraving - appeared to us from prehistoric and early times in Egypt some bodies that were not used to the effects of these periods or even on the effects of the following periods in historical times. These bodies varied greatly, which led the researcher to want to confine them and determine their purpose, which is what the current research aims at is whether they are related to political, religious, social or other purposes. These unfamiliar bodies will be dealt with applying to different body parts in order from top to bottom from head hair to toe in an attempt to accurately describe these bodies, then study them as a prelude to try to determine their purpose. Taking into account the initiation of men's bodies as the most common and widespread bodies and ending with women's bodies.
